content:
Apple released operating system updates today containing a large number of security fixes, and from the technical details published, it is evident that AI tools are rapidly advancing in the field of vulnerability research. The following are the details.

AI tools credited in Apple updates

Apple released earlier today:

  • iOS 26.6
  • iPadOS 26.6
  • macOS Tahoe 26.6
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8
  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8
  • tvOS 26.6
  • visionOS 26.6
  • watchOS 26.6

Following the release of the updates, Apple promptly updated its security release page, providing more information on a number of fixed issues, including the affected components and devices, potential impact, Apple's remediation methods, and the list of credited researchers.

One notable detail in today's documents is the considerable length, especially considering Apple released the 26.5.2 update less than a month ago and stated that it already included fixes originally slated for the 26.6 release cycle.

Another notable detail is that Anthropic researchers and Claude were credited for fixes involving WebKit, WebKit Storage, and WebDAV, some of which were completed in collaboration with researchers from Calif.io.

The same research team stated in May this year that, using Anthropic's Mythos Preview model, they built a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit on the M5 chip in just five days.

In every operating system update released today, Calif was credited for multiple kernel security fixes, involving a dozen or so researchers, indicating that multiple teams independently reported the same underlying issue.

In fact, Apple also fixed many other kernel vulnerabilities in this release cycle, with all of today's operating system updates listing a combined total of 30 independent CVEs.

It is worth mentioning that Apple has had access to Claude Mythos Preview through Anthropic's "Project Glasswing" programme since April this year. As a result, the number of vulnerabilities found internally through Claude may exceed what is reflected in public credits.

Finally, Anthropic is not the only AI company appearing in today's release notes. Apple also credited work by OpenAI Codex Security, Z.AI's GLM, and NVIDIA's AI Red Team, among others.

Although some names have appeared in last month's security release notes, today's updates further demonstrate how fast AI-assisted security research is developing, and reflect that companies must accelerate adjustments to their update schedules and bug bounty programmes to adapt to this new landscape.
